Paragraph:
Translation: Sanjaya said: Arjuna, having thus spoken on the battlefield, cast aside his bow and arrows and sat down on the chariot, his mind overwhelmed with grief.

Purport (Excerpt): While observing the situation of his enemy, Arjuna stood up on the chariot, but he was so afflicted with lamentation that he sat down again, setting aside his bow and arrows. Such a kind andsofthearted person, in the devotional service of the Lord, is fit to receive self-knowledge.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna has reached the climax of his psychological distress. He physically surrenders, casting down his weapons and collapsing onto his chariot seat, completely paralyzed by sorrow and mental torment.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna takes decisive physical action reflecting his internal collapse: he throws down his bow (Gandiva) and arrows. Sanjaya narrates this total abandonment of his martial duty.
Outcome/Resolution: Chapter 1 concludes with Arjuna in a state of absolute despondency (Vishada), setting the necessary stage of surrender and emptiness required before Krishna imparts the Bhagavad Gita.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Vishada (Deep despair and lamentation; the state that precedes true surrender)
Vairagya (A false or temporary renunciation driven by emotional trauma, not spiritual wisdom)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna's complete physical and emotional breakdown marks the end of his reliance on his own strength, intellect, and material reasoning. His utter devastation clears the slate, making him 'fit to receive self-knowledge' from Krishna in the subsequent chapters.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This is the climax of an acute stress reaction culminating in a total psychomotor collapse. Casting aside his bow is the final physical manifestation of a completely broken will and an overwhelmed mind. He is entirely consumed by grief and has lost all capacity to function.
